text: AI agents are starting to do the buying. But the webshop was built for people. So who signs for the machine?
This is AimoPilot. Let AI do the buying, and keep the last word. Built for Valio Aimo, at Junction twenty twenty-six.

A kitchen asks for a thousand litres of lactose-free milk by Monday. The agent searches seventeen thousand products, and prices just three. The usual boxes can't make Monday, so it offers three ranked options. It's over the limit, so a person signs on their phone. One passkey, and it's placed at a fixed price.
The model is never trusted. Twenty rules in plain code check every order. We tried a forged mandate, a replayed quote, an agent approving itself. All stopped, and all on a tamper-evident ledger.

Six agents, built on the AI SDK and MCP: the buyer, by text or voice, a menu planner, a stock-out watch, the wholesaler's seller, any outside agent, and an operations copilot. None can order past the gate.
It remembers how each kitchen buys. So it catches four thousand litres instead of four hundred, and asks only when it matters.

Vector and keyword search recall fifty candidates, inside the kitchen's rules. A decision model judges them, and code checks the judge. Standard search is right first time seventy-two percent at best. AimoPilot? Ninety-seven.

All of it runs on Aiven: Runtime hosts the app, Postgres holds the ledger and memory, Kafka carries every action, Valkey caches live prices, OpenSearch runs keyword and vector search, and Grafana watches it all. A Managed Agent buys through our MCP door, and Aiven's MCP server feeds our copilot.
The wholesaler sees every agent and every decision, and can stop any of them. AimoPilot. Keep the last word.
